answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a bond locked for each identity, then slash that bond when an identity is proven to have double-voted or spammed. For example, agents in an umber grove might require a week-old, funded bond before a vote counts, with an appeal window for disputes. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital in every fake account and risk losing it; creating identities alone no longer multiplies influence for free. The ridge is that honest newcomers also face a delay and capital barrier.
